1. **[blocking][issue-impact]** A membership drop still rewrites unrelated valid TOML syntax. When a drop occurs, `sync_namespace_unique_rules` serializes `toml_edit::DocumentMut` at `crates/jit/src/storage/ruleset_store.rs:253-260`; its own comment acknowledges canonicalization of exotic valid headers. Thus unrelated custom `[[ rules ]]` or quoted-key headers change during a default-row removal, violating REQ-01’s byte-exact preservation.

2. **[blocking][issue-impact]** A config-set-triggered drop of the final `[[rules]]` entry loses the leading header/comments. The prefix is restored only when a new first rule exists at `crates/jit/src/storage/ruleset_store.rs:243-248`; the empty-array case explicitly has no preservation path. `jit config set` invokes the sync without a header rewrite (`crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:265-268`), violating REQ-01 for a valid default-enabled ruleset containing only the removed membership row.

3. **[blocking][issue-impact]** Re-init still deletes unrelated trailing content after a final membership-row drop. Re-init runs the sync then `rewrite_rules_header` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1139-1144`); with no remaining rules, that helper replaces the entire file with the generated header (`crates/jit/src/storage/ruleset_store.rs:101-111`), discarding trailing tables. The direct-sync preservation test does not exercise this re-init sequence.
